item.title: Swedish word of the day: snus
item.description: There are fewer things more Swedish than snus, the small nicotine pouches wedged under the lips of one in seven Swedes. But where does the word snus actually come from?

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Friday
item.description: Sweden Democrat leader willing to delay PR revocation law, Sweden to develop air raid warning app, government unveils new prison conditions for teens and more news from Sweden on Friday.

item.title: Sweden unveils new prison conditions for teenagers
item.description: The Swedish government has revealed conditions for young teenagers, aged 13-15, who will be sentenced to prison from July of this year.

item.title: Sweden Democrats open to delaying PR revocation law
item.description: Sweden Democrat leader Jimmie Åkesson has said that he is willing to delay a proposed law that would see as many as 185,000 people stripped of permanent residency until after the election in September.

item.title: Sweden pledges 12.9 billion kronor for Ukraine air defence
item.description: The 12.9 billion kronor in military aid for Ukraine is focused primarily on air defence capabilities.

item.title: Swedish government considering language screening for young children
item.description: Sweden’s government wants to investigate the possibility of introducing tests to screen the Swedish skills of young children to make sure they can speak the language sufficiently before starting school or preschool.

item.title: Can dual national Brits travel to UK without valid British passport after all?
item.description: Upcoming rule changes to the UK's new ETA border system have angered dual national Brits, but updated travel guidance from the government and a major airline suggests those without valid British passports may be allowed entry - as long as they have an expired UK passport.

item.title: Swedish word of the day: magsjuka
item.description: Today's word is the scourge of Swedish winters.

item.title: Sweden's Social Democrats say yes to chemical castration of pedophiles
item.description: The Social Democrats, Sweden's largest opposition party, has put its support behind a right-wing proposal to chemically castrate pedophiles.

item.title: Sweden's opposition parties demand law to stop teenage deportations
item.description: The Green Party has presented a new proposal to stop teenage deportations. This time, it is supported by a united opposition. "The government must act now," wrote Social Democrat spokesperson Ida Karkiainen in a statement.
